content: When conducting a research priority-setting exercise, it is essential to clearly define the roles of researchers and participants, ensuring that priorities are appropriately separated and addressed. A systematic approach should be employed to undertake a research priority-setting exercise. This involves structured guidance for staff, particularly in the context of the World Health Organization (WHO). Phase 3: Publish At this stage, you must develop a comprehensive publication and dissemination plan. This plan is critical to ensure that the research priorities are widely recognized, adopted, and implemented effectively. Developing a Publication and Dissemination Strategy It is important to ensure that your reporting includes the following key elements: The objectives of the research; The context in which the research was conducted; The methods used to establish priorities; The identified research priorities; The implementation plan for these priorities; and The monitoring and evaluation plan to assess progress and outcomes. Additionally, you should determine whether an academic paper will be produced. If so, ensure that it complies with the WHO Open Access Policy to facilitate accessibility and transparency. Annex 1: A Systematic Approach to Research Priority-Setting Phase 4: Monitor and Evaluate In this phase, you must create a plan to measure the impact of the research priorities on the original objectives. Typically, this involves assessing improvements in public health outcomes. These improvements may be evaluated through metrics such as increased awareness, uptake, implementation, translation, and the overall impact of the research priorities.
